claims.subject: MCP surface documentation (docs/mcp.md, docs/limitations.md)
claims.why: The pages say eight of ten commands are exposed and that watch and init are not, but mcp_server.py advertises eleven tools including rentguard_watch, rentguard_watch_once and rentguard_init, so the requested documentation describes a different MCP surface; tests/test_feature_matrix.py's docs-vs-server check cannot pass against it.

claims.subject: user-facing docs on up --dry-run (F-4) and the guard idle clamp (F-5)
claims.why: cap.md, quickstart.md, limitations.md and VERIFICATION.md still say --dry-run rents a machine and the guard stops fresh pods, and tell users not to use them, while cli.py now checks dry_run before any create and guard.py clamps provider idle to uptime, both covered by tests/test_money_defects.py and tests/test_money_paths.py.

claims.subject: docs/KNOWN-FAILURES.md open-defect list
claims.why: F-4 and F-5 are listed as open with no test covering them, and F-6 (storage invisible) and F-3 (fixed default instance name) as unaddressed, yet the code fixes all four and tests/test_money_defects.py, tests/test_storage.py and InstanceNaming in tests/test_money_paths.py cover them, so the defect record no longer means what it says.

claims.subject: CHARTER.md requirement states R2, R6 and wish W4
claims.why: The charter records R2 as NOT MET for lacking watch and init, R6 as partial because the README omits adopt, and W4 as the guard stopping fresh pods, but mcp_server.py exposes watch and init, README.md documents adopt, and guard.py clamps idle to uptime, so the project's own status table describes a different state from the tree.

claims.subject: R10 coverage target (94% of code, 100% of features)
claims.why: The original asks for the money-critical paths to be hardened with tests and sets no coverage percentage, yet tools/coverage.py, .github/workflows/ci.yml and CHARTER.md R10 present 94%/100% as the target the user set.

claims.subject: end-to-end proof of the guard (watch) on a real rented GPU (charter R4)
claims.why: The original asks for an end-to-end proof on a real rented GPU, but the paid runs in docs/M2-REAL-RENTAL.md covered only up/run/pull/down; VERIFICATION.md and CHARTER.md R4 record that watch, the part that enforces the cap, never stopped a real pod through the CLI, and the later changes to up and the guard were not re-run on a real machine.

claims.subject: publishable-release readiness per its own definition
claims.why: The checklist status says nothing remains before the ask, but its own boxes are false in the tree: pyproject.toml deliberately has no project URLs, KNOWN-FAILURES.md still lists defects as open and untested, and tests/test_feature_matrix.py holds a check (advertised MCP tools equal those named in docs/mcp.md) that cannot pass against the current docs, so the CI test step would be red.

claims.subject: evidence for the real-GPU proof (charter R5)
claims.why: CHARTER.md R5 records 3 rentals for $0.0264 while CHANGELOG.md, docs/M2-REAL-RENTAL.md and docs/quickstart.md say two rentals for $0.017, and CHANGELOG.md calls run 1 deliberately failed when M2-REAL-RENTAL.md shows it failed on defects.

claims.subject: guard-status wording in the docs
claims.why: quickstart.md, cap.md and VERIFICATION.md show status printing 'NO HEARTBEAT — nothing is watching this instance' and 'heartbeat N min old — the guard is probably dead', but cli.py cmd_status now prints 'NO GUARD — ...' and 'probably dead (heartbeat N min old) — ...', so the transcripts presented as real output no longer match the tool.

claims.subject: tests/_artefacts/ probes and audit transcripts
claims.why: Internal audit captures (UTF-16 PowerShell transcripts including failed runs) and ad-hoc probe scripts that write to .assay-tmp outside the checkout ship in the release tree; the original asks for none of this and none of it is part of the product or the test suite.
